answer.read: Family foundry (sup:70110) that historically accepted prices below full cost (EV-2023) and expects partnership (doc M3). It wants cash fast (doc M2 asked for short payment) and already took our 14-day terms, dropping from €138.55 to €134.00 after conceding our should-cost and notice-period points. Its should-cost range (€126-133) suggests margin is thin, so the stabilise relationship charge matters. Its delivery and quality are weak (sc:70110@2026Q3 amber, OTD 85.2%, open 8D), which gives us leverage. Its offer is still open, not final, and it is conceding about €3.78 per reply.
answer.message: Thank you for your revised proposal and for acknowledging the cost and notice-period points. Since prices under our framework are fixed per calendar year, we propose that any adjustment start at the turn of the year, combined with the fast payment you asked for. This gives you a fair increase on a sound basis. Given the current delivery performance, we think this is a balanced step toward a stable partnership.
answer.reason: o2 has the lowest C of all options, about the same as E0, and moves the effective date to January. That is consistent with the verified contract clause and gives the supplier a cleaner story, while 14-day payment meets its stated liquidity wish. A price below health avoids pushing too far, though the supplier will likely counter, and the offer is not final, so we keep pressing rather than accept €134. Delivery record and order history are new argument kinds that support restraint.
